title: Hurricane Maria: Blue Roof Relief (no graphics)
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers installs the first temporary Blue Roof on a home in Ponce; Puerto Rico's second largest city. Interviews with: Carmen Carlo/Homeowner, CPT John Rossi/USACE-St. Louis District
keywords: Maria, Ponce, blue, Hurricane Maria, VIPR, USACE, engineers, Hurricane, roof, Puerto Rico
unit_name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Omaha District

transcript.text: (upbeat music)
- [Narrator] Since Hurricane Maria decimated Puerto Rico,
the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers has installed
more than 4,000 temporary blue roofs.
It's estimated that there are 60,000 homes
throughout the island in need of this temporary fix.
This house is the first home in Ponce,
Puerto Rico's second largest city,
to have a blue roof installed.
- We believe we are gonna lose everything.
Because the thing is if we don't cover what we have,
we gonna lose it.
I know it, and I understand it's not easy.
But I said, wow the families around here
we gotta do something, we gotta have peace.
We've gotta have at least a little bit of peace.
Even though we don't have light.
But we can live without it.
But the thing is if you lose what you have inside your house
then you gonna be worse.
Because it's not easy.
Let me tell you it's not.
- [Narrator] To get residents in need
signed up for the program, a little bit of legwork
had to be put in first.
- For Puerto Rico it was a little bit different.
They don't really have a defined address system
in some of the rural areas.
So we start going door to door.
We talk to the people in Puerto Rico.
We talk to the residents who have damaged homes.
We tell them about our program.
- [Narrator] To be eligible for the blue roof program
a home must have less than 50% structural damage.
The temporary covering not only prevents further damage
to the property, it also reduces temporary housing costs
by allowing residents to remain in their homes
while recovering from the storm.
But the biggest benefit of the program?
- Relief.
They know that people are here to help them.
Especially once they see the blue roofs going on
in their neighborhood, they know that it's coming soon.
And they're grateful and they're relieved.
So we're here trying to help put people back in their homes,
give them a place to call their home that they can rebuild
and start getting their lives back to normalcy.
So it's starting today here in Ponce
with this house right here.
- We feel a little bit peace
now that we seen you people around.
- [Narrator] With roofs now going on in Ponce,
the program will continue to expand throughout the island.
Mike Lash, U.S. Army Corp of Engineers, Puerto Rico.
